sql:
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
       lh.name AS hold_name,
       LEFT(lh.reason, 200) AS reason_truncated,
       lh.entity_table AS entity_table_scope,
       lh.subject_user_id,
       lh.is_active,
       CAST(lh.placed_at AS date) AS placed_at_date,
       CAST(lh.released_at AS date) AS released_at_date,
       CASE WHEN lh.is_active THEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lh.placed_at AS date)) END AS days_since_placed
FROM legal_holds lh
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = lh.tenant_id
ORDER BY lh.is_active DESC, lh.placed_at ASC, lh.id ASC

text:
Submitted. Summary of what the report does:

- **Grain:** one row per `legal_holds` record.
- **Columns:** tenant name, hold name, truncated reason (200 chars), entity table scope, subject user id, is_active, placed_at date, released_at date (blank if still active), and days since placed (computed only for active holds, using the fixed date 2026-01-05).
- **Ordering:** active holds first, then oldest `placed_at` first within each group — so any stale, long-open holds surface at the top.
- **Note to analyst:** I didn't impose a manual row limit; the standard reporting cap (50 rows) and its automatic total-row count will tell us whether the active+released holds exceed that and warrant a narrower follow-up query (e.g., active-only).
